lines: The core laboratory is barely recognizable as a man-made space. The walls are alive — root networks thick as cables form a lattice over every surface, pulsing with green bioluminescence. The air is heavy with warmth rising from geothermal vents below.

At the center of the chamber, a massive growth pod dominates the room. It towers over the surrounding equipment, its trunk a fusion of engineered plant tissue and consumed lab machinery. Sol-reactive veins glow along its surface.
This is the Apex specimen — Batch 7's alpha organism. Everything else in the bio-labs grew from this. It senses your approach, and the roots along the floor begin to shift.
The Apex Overgrowth shudders and collapses inward, its massive trunk splitting open. Instead of sap, light pours from the wound — concentrated sol energy stored in the organism's vascular system.
Throughout the lab, you can feel the secondary growth systems faltering. Without the alpha's root network sustaining them, the rogue specimens will wither within weeks.
Among the remains, intact tissue samples glow with stable bio-circuitry — the technology Project Verdant was meant to create, perfected by years of autonomous evolution.
GREENWAY AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES — DR. TOVA AREN, PERSONAL LOG
'I came back. The Council doesn't know. The growth hasn't stopped — it's accelerated. The alpha specimen has consumed the entire core lab infrastructure.'
'But the tissue samples... they're perfect. Stable bio-circuitry grown from living plant matter. Sol components that breathe, that heal, that grow stronger over time.'
'This is what the Greenway was supposed to give the Ring. Not just food. Living technology. I just need more time to understand it.'
GREENWAY AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES — AUTOMATED GROWTH LOG
'Year 1: Root network extends through 60% of facility. Growth rate: 2.3 cm/day.'
'Year 2: Root network reaches geothermal tap. Growth rate increases to 8.7 cm/day. Alpha specimen mass: 400 kg. New specimens budding from secondary root nodes.'
'Year 3: Facility saturation at 94%. Alpha specimen mass: estimated 2,200 kg. Automated systems failing as root infiltration shorts power conduits. This will be the final automated entry.'
